# agents/antigravity/ — the Antigravity adapter

**The verb table in AGENTS.md is the adapter.** Google Antigravity reads `AGENTS.md` in
the project root as project rules (alongside `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/rules/`), so mova's
verb table routes every phrase to its playbook with no generated files. An instance
configured `agent: antigravity` gets nothing generated here, and `docs/agents.test.ts`
checks instead that AGENTS.md's verb table links every active playbook.

## Optional workflow shims — supported, not generated by default

Antigravity supports **workflows**: markdown files in the project's `.agents/workflows/`
directory, invoked as `/<workflow-name>` slash commands. A pointer-only workflow per verb
(`.agents/workflows/mova-<verb>.md`, body: *Follow playbooks/<verb>.md. All rules live
there and in `docs/mechanics/` — this file deliberately holds none.*) would add explicit
slash invocation on top of the AGENTS.md routing — the same layering as the Claude Code
and opencode adapters.

Setup does not generate these by default because the format details below are only
lightly verified; a human (or a later template release, once the format is pinned) can add
them. If you do, keep them pointers — a rule copied into a shim is a rule free to drift.

## What is verified vs assumed

Verified via Antigravity's docs and current guides (antigravity.google/docs/rules-workflows,
checked 2026-08-13): AGENTS.md is read as project rules; workflows are project markdown
files invoked as slash commands. **Assumed / lightly verified:** the exact directory
(`.agents/workflows/` — guides also show an older `.agent/` spelling with backward
support) and whether workflow files take frontmatter. The honest minimum stands:
AGENTS.md carries this agent; everything else is optional sugar.
